spec_match.rationale: The entire demo uses the long-standing SVG pathLength ATTRIBUTE — the CSS path-length property this v149 feature ships never appears in the markup, styles or generated code, so the page demonstrates the pre-existing attribute rather than the feature.

interactive.rationale: Animate-all, reset, a duration slider with readout, measured px-length labels and a live measurement table are real interactions (assessed from code review and the rendered DOM; the controls were not driven in this session).

blurb_alignment.rationale: The page matches its own framing, but as part of the css-path-length feature it tells the attribute story; the index card's promise of demonstrating the CSS property's benefit is only implied, never shown.

edge_cases.rationale: Real getTotalLength() measurements ground the comparison, but there is no CSS-property variant, no reduced-motion handling, and the initial state renders six blank shape boxes until Animate is pressed.

references.rationale: The ChromeStatus link points at feature 5756349891821568, not this folder's identity 4861677550043136 — a wrong-id reference that would mislead the slug self-heal script.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite probes the real CSS property contract and honestly fails 4 of 6 in this browser; notably none of this page's behaviour depends on those assertions, confirming the page is off-surface.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Cloud-fallback observation only, NOT browser-verified per auto-research.md §0 — headless Chromium 141 (full-page screenshot + DOM, not chrome-devtools-mcp): lengths table populated with measured values (circle 238px, star 311px, …) proving the attribute path works here; shapes are blank at rest and the animation was not driven. chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session (the auto-research.md section-0 blocker applies, so this is NOT browser verification): what was exercised is page load, full-page screenshot read, served/dumped DOM state and the /conformance/ route result; driving every control and capturing console/network evidence remains for an MCP-equipped session.

design_system.rationale: Variables throughout; .btn and .btn.primary set background and color together.

accessibility.rationale: The duration slider has an aria-label and readout and the table is labelled, but all six SVGs share the useless duplicate aria-label 'Demo SVG graphic', the draw animation ignores prefers-reduced-motion, and completion is only visible via the progress bar.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Cards wrap and the table is narrow; clean at 1280px headless, though the five-column table may pinch at ≈360px (untested).

openQuestions.title: Demonstrate the CSS path-length property — the page currently shows only the old attribute
openQuestions.detail: Every shape uses pathLength="100" markup, which has worked for years; the v149 feature is path-length as a CSS property (set from a stylesheet, no per-element markup). Add a third column/mode where the paths carry NO attribute and a single `.draw-path { path-length: 100 }` rule does the normalisation — with CSS.supports('path-length','100') detection and the standard unsupported banner, since this browser fails that probe. That contrast (attribute vs property) is exactly this concept's reason to exist.

openQuestions.title: Correct the ChromeStatus reference to feature 4861677550043136
openQuestions.detail: The see-also links chromestatus.com/feature/5756349891821568; the feature index and conformance suite identify this folder as 4861677550043136. Wrong ids break the self-heal recovery path.

openQuestions.title: Give the resting state something to see
openQuestions.detail: With stroke-dashoffset:100 at load, all six cards render as empty boxes until Animate is pressed (screenshot evidence). Show a faint ghost stroke (as draw-on-path does) or start the shapes drawn with Animate replaying the draw.

openQuestions.title: Deduplicate SVG labels and respect reduced motion
openQuestions.detail: Name each SVG for its shape ('Circle draw animation'), and under prefers-reduced-motion jump the draw to its end state instead of animating; announce completion via the existing progress row with role=status.

summary: Reviewed with the headless-Chromium-141 cloud fallback (not chrome-devtools-mcp): full-page screenshot + DOM of /v149/css-path-length/multi-path-sync/ and the feature /conformance/ route (HTTP 200; panel 2 pass / 4 fail / 0 blocked). The synchronisation story is well told and fully functional here — because it never touches the v149 surface: everything rides the legacy pathLength attribute, the CSS property is absent from the page, and the ChromeStatus link carries a wrong feature id. The lengths table proves real measurement; the animation itself was not driven headless.
